children: reported an 11% increase in October vehicle sales, extending its growth streak to six consecutive months as surging overseas shipments helped offset sluggish domestic demand and fierce price competition.

BYD sold 490,168 vehicles during the month, compared with a 17% year-over-year sales increase in September. Overseas shipments more than doubled, climbing 102.8% to 170,194 vehicles, according to Reuters calculations based on company figures released Sunday.

For investors, the results highlight BYD's growing dependence on international markets to sustain sales growth as China's automotive industry struggles with weak consumer demand and aggressive discounting. Although exports provide an important growth opportunity, increasing competition and potential trade restrictions could pressure profitability.
The October figures follow BYD's third-quarter earnings report, which showed profit growth slowing to 28% from a year earlier, falling short of analysts' expectations.
Reuters reported that the broader Chinese automotive industry's push into export markets is intensifying competition internationally, even as manufacturers contend with difficult conditions at home.

BYD also faces potential regulatory challenges in Europe, where it ranks among the leading exporters of hybrid vehicles. A proposed China-European Union agreement aimed at restricting hybrid imports could create additional obstacles to the company's international expansion.
China's domestic automotive market is expected to recover modestly in 2027 following a sharper-than-anticipated downturn this year.

The outlook leaves BYD balancing rapid international expansion against mounting competitive and regulatory pressures, with investors watching whether higher overseas sales can translate into sustained earnings growth.

title: BYD's October vehicle sales rise as overseas demand offsets China weakness
